 Washington Wizards Detroit Pistons The Detroit Pistons are once again in the mix for the No. 1 seed in the Eastern Conference, winning seven of their first 10 games, including a win over the Washington Wizards on Monday.

 Detroit has been off since then, and it’ll have a major rest advantage on Thursday night in a rematch with the Wizards.

 Washington lost against the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday, though it did have Anthony Davis in the lineup. Davis has missed a couple games this season, and he could end up sitting out the back end of a back-to-back as the Wizards look to manage his workload.

 Despite that, oddsmakers have set the Pistons 10.5-point favorites on the road against the struggling Wizards. Washington has dropped five consecutive games, falling under .500 in the 2026-27 season.

--> The Pistons picked up an 11-point win over Washington on Monday, and they have a major rest advantage heading into Thursday’s matchup.
 Detroit was able to beat Washington despite 44 points from Anthony Davis, and there’s a chance the Wizards end up resting the veteran forward on the second night of a back-to-back after losing to Indiana on Wednesday. 
--> Detroit was able to beat Washington despite 44 points from Anthony Davis, and there’s a chance the Wizards end up resting the veteran forward on the second night of a back-to-back after losing to Indiana on Wednesday. 
 Washington has dropped five games in a row, and it has fallen to just 23rd in the NBA in net rating. The Wizards’ defense has been decent (17th in defensive rating), but the team is just 26th in offense and now has to take on a Pistons team that is third in the league in defensive rating and sixth in net rating.
